verdictStatement: Both of my v2 findings are fixed at the site rather than around it, which is the distinction that decided the last two rounds. The roster now names /sliceStanding, and I confirmed the claim rather than the promise: 52 changed leaf paths, every one rostered, zero escapees — and in the converse direction the single instance of padding, /date, is declared in the roster sentence itself, so the closure claim cannot be caught out in either direction. The universal survives testing too, with /honestyRepairsFromV1 and the three unrostered /proposedBroker sub-paths byte-identical to v2. firstSlice now reads 'Absence of a SATISFIED DR-108', the exact one-word repair I named, and I searched the whole document: 'sealed DR-108' survives at one location only, inside an attack instruction telling a reviewer to hunt for it. The file 02 must-not is no longer described but carried, both lines byte-exact, the full operative sentence intact including the bypass clause, with the artifact declining the temptation to quote only the convenient fragment. The measurement discipline is the strongest I have seen in this corpus: three remeasurement blocks, eleven digest entries, every one byte-exact against the commit its block names, two labelled historical and one LIVE, with governingSources deferring to the LIVE block by name instead of asserting a live adjective that can go stale. I pressed on the places a passing artifact usually hides a defect and found none. The re-pinned COORD is the real hazard when a successor updates a moving source, so I re-verified the named properties in the new bytes rather than inheriting my earlier check — D-096 (A) still unsatisfied, D-002's DR-108 deferral still present, slice name intact. D-110 does not touch file 08 and mentions DR-108 only to deny satisfying it. The v1 containment repair did not regress under the new edits, and both its routing targets still exist. The dispatch offered a PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT allowance for COORD drift and it was not needed, because COORD has not moved since the measurement. What remains is two advisories, neither chargeable. The v1 repair list still carries the 'no sealed-row claim' sentence that my v2 review found incomplete, and it is the one historical object that did not get a standing label in the pass that labelled the others — but leaving it byte-unchanged is what the roster universal requires and what a historical record should do, the document self-corrects for anyone reading the succession, and the underlying defect is now actually fixed, so no open obligation goes uncarried. That last point is the whole of the severity difference from v2, and it is a principled line rather than a lenient one.

coordinatorNote: ACCEPT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-108 stays OPEN at file 08 line 290; I did not touch file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, marked nothing SATISFIED, invented no keychain/file/broker API, minted no D-096 (A) grant, and did not commit. Accepting the candidate is not sealing it — its own DO-NOT-SEAL stands, and recording it is a separate coordinator act under MF-6. Five things to weigh. First, the direction across three rounds is clean and monotone: v1 minted an unsourced containment guarantee, v2 fixed the substance but broke its own bookkeeping in two places, v3 fixes the bookkeeping without regressing the substance — I re-verified the v1 repair rather than assuming it held. Second, both remaining advisories are carryable and neither needs a v4; the first is repairable by a purely additive standing label if a v4 happens for other reasons, and explicitly should NOT be repaired by editing the historical list, which would falsify the record of what v2 claimed. Third, the independence limitation matters for scope: I have never read any Codex verdict in this series, so the artifact's account of CODEX-SSCV2-S1/A1/A2/A3 is digest-matched but content-unverified by me — I judged those repairs on the bytes, and CODEX-SSCV2-A3 in particular I could only confirm on its face. If the coordinator needs that lane's findings confirmed as addressed, it needs the Codex lane. Fourth, a note on the standing rule the dispatch supplied: PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT for append-only COORD was not exercised here, since COORD has not moved since the artifact's remeasurement — the rule is available for a future round, not load-bearing in this one. Fifth, this artifact's remeasurement pattern — multiple blocks, each labelled with a standing and each naming the HEAD it was taken at — is the cleanest solution to the pin-staleness problem I have measured anywhere in this corpus, where every other artifact family still carries at least one stale governing pin. It is worth propagating as convention.
